config.prompt:
Answer the question using only the meeting excerpts below.
A shortened participant identifier matches a speaker label ending in that identifier; for example, A matches Grad A.
For questions about what a participant thought, use their relevant statements, questions, and suggestions.
Make sure to include every relevant detail supported by the excerpts - every missed detail is penalized.
Say that the evidence is insufficient only when it contains no relevant information.
Give a concise, direct answer.

questions.question: What did the Prime Minister say about fraud in distribution of funds?
questions.reference_answer: The Prime Minister was adamant that fraud was unacceptable and reiterated that fraudsters would have to return the money. Nonetheless, the government's priority remained the speedy disbursement of funds to those that were in need.

oracle.answer: The Prime Minister stated that while the priority was to get money out quickly to Canadians who needed it, fraud is unacceptable. He mentioned that there are measures in place to detect fraud and that all fraudsters will be required to pay back the money they received fraudulently. He reiterated that safeguards are in place to ensure fraudulent recipients repay the money.

questions.question: What did the Minister of Seniors say about pandemic assistance for seniors?
questions.reference_answer: The Minister of Seniors clarified that his office recognizes that seniors are in great need. The minister explained that those receiving OAS and GIS are getting payments of $200 and $300 respectively. The minister was insistent that this was not an insignificant amount.

oracle.answer: The Minister of Seniors stated that the government is providing support for Canadian seniors during the pandemic by introducing a one-time tax-free payment of $300 for those who receive Old Age Security (OAS) and $200 for those receiving Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), totaling $500 for seniors who receive both. Additionally, the government is supporting community-based projects to improve the quality of life for seniors through the New Horizons for Seniors program and investing in other charities. The Minister emphasized that seniors need help and the government is taking action to provide greater financial security during the crisis.

questions.question: What did the Prime Minister say about students?
questions.reference_answer: The Prime Minister clarified that while young people are in need of funds, especially due to loss of income over the summer, they are also in need of work experience. The government would start providing the Canada emergency student benefit which will assist in this by making both jobs and money available.

oracle.answer: The Prime Minister said that students need both money and work experience. He mentioned setting up programs such as Canada summer jobs and another program with 76,000 new jobs for young people in important sectors to address the gaps in the labor market. He emphasized continuing to work with youth and employers to ensure that young people are well-supported despite the unprecedented situation. Additionally, he acknowledged the necessity of providing support for students who cannot find jobs.

questions.question: What did Bains say about business loans?
questions.reference_answer: Bains said that the government has been accommodating of small businesses in the past and it will continue to do so. The government has increased the threshold for individual companies and looks forward to making further adjustments. Bains emphasized that 590,000 loans have already been distributed through the CEBA program, highlighting its efficacy.

oracle.answer: Bains mentioned that the government has shown flexibility in the eligibility criteria for business loans, specifically decreasing the payroll threshold for individual companies applying for the CEBA loan from $50,000 to $20,000 and increasing the upper limit from $1 million to $1.5 million. He assured that they are looking into issues related to business loans and will continue to bring forward necessary changes to ensure more businesses can access the support they need.

questions.question: What did Morneau say about the debt?
questions.reference_answer: Morneau explained that the government was committed to supporting Canadians. It came into the pandemic with a strong fiscal position, and while the pandemic will bring challenges, it will face those challenges while supporting small businesses and Canadians.

oracle.answer: Morneau did not provide specific details about the debt servicing cost or directly address the $1 trillion debt figure mentioned. Instead, he emphasized the government's commitment to supporting Canadians during challenging times, stating that they will continue to focus on the well-being of all Canadians. He also indicated that there would be an opportunity to provide a full outline of the costs and benefits of their measures when appropriate.

questions.question: What did Bains say about the threshold for the wage subsidy program and loan refinancing?
questions.reference_answer: Bains said that the threshold for the program had been lowered to a 15% decline in revenue from a 30% decline. Businesses will also be able to compare losses to more recent time periods due to greater flexibility. Bain clarified that the government is listening to businesses and recognizes its need to be agile.

oracle.answer: Bains stated that the threshold for the wage subsidy program was reduced from 30% to 15% decline in revenue. Businesses can now use either January and February as a reference period to demonstrate revenue losses or compare to the same time last year. There is no specific mention of loan refinancing in Bains' statement.

questions.question: What did Bains say about the arts, culture, and tourism industry?
questions.reference_answer: Bains claimed that the government was aware of these issues and had allocated $500 million to arts and culture organizations. Bains also explained that while pandemic control efforts were affecting these industries adversely, Canadians' health and safety remained the government's priority.

oracle.answer: Bains stated that the government understands the importance of arts, heritage, and sports organizations to communities and has allocated $500 million to address their specific financial needs to help them become more resilient during the difficult time. This funding was recently rolled out, and the government looks forward to engaging with communities across the country.
